function: DRL agent sets beamforming power (MRT/ZF directions), DC bias, RSMA common rates and IRS element alignment to maximize secrecy energy efficiency (p. 7).
system: Indoor VLC MISO downlink: 6 LEDs, 2 single-photodetector users, 1 eavesdropper, passive mirror-array reflecting IRS of 16 elements, visible light band, 6x6x3 m room (pp. 4, 9).
method: Actor-critic deep reinforcement learning (dual-sampling PPO with GAE), two hidden layers of 256 units, online training by interaction with simulated environment (pp. 8-10).
data_channel: Custom simulated VLC channel: Lambertian LoS gains plus specular IRS NLoS paths from room geometry; users and eavesdropper randomly placed; no dataset or measurements (pp. 4-5, 9).
test_conditions: Trained and evaluated in one simulated room (default 6 LEDs, 2 users, 16 IRS elements); sweeps of IRS elements, users, power, QoS, Eve position; no separate test (pp. 9-13).
baselines: PPO [51], DDPG [52], epsilon-Greedy (no neural network), MRT-design after [53] (MRT beamforming only); also RSMA versus SDMA and with versus without IRS (pp. 11-12).
metrics: Secrecy energy efficiency (bit/Hz/J), average reward, per-user achievable rate, total power consumption, average time cost per step (pp. 10-12).
complexity: Order O(sum_p m_(p-1) m_p) over network layers, p. 9 (Remark 2); average time cost per step in ms versus users and IRS elements, p. 11 (Fig. 6).
q1_support: p. 4: "Since LED transmitters typically conform to the Lambertian model" - the channel is a custom geometric Lambertian LoS plus specular IRS model (Eqs. 4-10); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 10: "For the actor network, the input dimension is N LK + 5K + L + 3" - network size is tied to N, K and L, and the paper only sweeps these parameters (Figs. 7-10, pp. 11-13); no test in conditions unseen in training, fine-tuning or transfer is reported.
q3_support: p. 11: "ε-Greedy exhibits the lowest time cost as it does not involve neural networks" - non-neural greedy baseline; learned baselines are DDPG [52] and PPO [51], and DS-PPO has higher SEE than all in Fig. 5 (p. 11) and than DDPG in Fig. 10 (p. 12).
q4_support: p. 9: "Remark 2: The computational complexity of the proposed DS-PPO approach" - stated as O of the sum over layers of m(p-1) times m(p); Fig. 6 (p. 11) also reports average time cost per step.
q5_support: p. 9: "The detailed simulation settings are summarized in Table II" - only simulation parameters are given; no code or data link, and no public dataset, is stated anywhere in the paper.
notes: VLC system with an optical (mirror-array) IRS; the learned part outputs power, DC bias, common rates and IRS alignment, while beamforming directions come from MRT/ZF (p. 7), so area 3. q3 caveat for the reviewer: the only non-learned baseline is epsilon-Greedy (p. 11: the agent explores the action to maximize SEE each step; paper says it has no neural networks, yet Fig. 5 draws it as a curve over training steps); PPO lacks the dual sampling and GAE of DS-PPO (ablation-like), so DDPG is the learned baseline. q1: the Lambertian VLC model is a textbook custom model, not a standard one. q2: the paper does not say whether the agent is retrained at each sweep point.
